description: Green firework starts the race: cacophony of roaring engines, car crashes and explosions; barricades, train, truck and wrecking balls produce surround and height effects; T-Rex stomps and roars in the top layer with vigorous LF; King Kong leaps from building to building.

Hubble Space Telescope hardware upgrade scene: deafening silence of space against dialogue lines with Houston; debris cloud warning, Steven Price's score builds tension, then debris strikes and voices swirl chaotically from speaker to speaker.

Voices, music and engine rumblings open the credits; Mad Max is chased, the camera stays still as he disappears, silence falls, then a car launches overhead as ghosts of his past whisper from the sides and heights.

Engine roars in shadow, deep LF grumble, high-speed chase: bumps, crashes, screeching tires, passing traffic and horns through the surrounds with some height activity; inside the Penguin's car as it rolls, swirling glass-shattering effects, finishing on Giacchino's Batman theme.

Evelyn steps on a nail and drops a picture frame which shatters with piano-chord LF impact; she switches on the exterior red emergency lights as the monster's breathing/steps move from top-left to top-right height channels, then descend through the stairs to front-left/side/rear surround. Heavy bass throughout.

Bomber aircraft fly overhead with loud engine drone in heights; inside the aircraft, wind, turbulence, fuselage creaks, intense flak object-based explosions around the room, fighter planes whizzing with spatial accuracy and heavy gunfire booming through the subwoofer.

Paul and his father fly the ornithopter to oversee the spice harvest, with beating wings and ambient hum, then a dive down to assist. Paul steps onto the sand, granular dust running through his fingers, as the sandworm emerges and they make a mad dash back to the craft.
Atmos remix of the Normandy beach landing, with every gunshot precisely placed and the full chaos of the assault wrapping around the room. One of cinema's most relentless sound sequences.

Climactic canyon trench run: low bass from jet engines, heights and surrounds as the jets curve through the canyon, bombs on the bunker, then a missile evade with flares; the flare-versus-missile impacts are a standout effect.

Longer than a typical demo clip but covers everything Atmos does well: gunshots, screeching tires, driving action; audio is present from the sides, mimicking what Baby hears when his headphones drown out his tinnitus.

Convoy races into a massive sand-and-lightning cyclone that whistles and roars around the room; a vehicle gets swept into a vortex, spins around the room and is thrown over the listener's head into the back wall. Scene ends as Max is thrown from his vehicle and blacks out.
Heights engage from the very start. The score wraps around the listener and ties into the spacecraft flight, fully immersing you in the sci-fi world.

Cruise hangs from the swing-load under the H125 helicopter, thunderous blade slap through the heights; Cavill's machine gun blasts from the LF as bullets whip past in the surrounds; a dramatic end with warning alarms and both helicopters coming down.

Mach 10 test flight: subtle tension build during prep (treadmill, gear), then jet engines fire with a rumble, roof of the shack blows off, quiet/muted in-cockpit audio, climax with the faint distant explosion.

Chapter 8/9 (Extras: Complete Live Aid performance). Freddie sits at the piano for the second half of 'We Are The Champions'; the crowd joins louder with each verse until a cathartic wave rolls through stadium and cinema alike.
Burning town: collapsing structures, distant footsteps and ricochets land in their own spaces; fire crackles overhead with walls closing in.
When they first go into no-man's-land: five minutes of very quiet build-up while the soldiers try to stay silent, then planes slowly get louder and louder and fly right overhead.
The film's opening seconds: planes flying and fighting overhead, helicopters swirling, PA announcements and master-caution alarms. The overhead flyover that Atmos owners love.
The lobby shootout from the 4K Atmos remaster: Trinity's wall-run flip with great height movement, the elevator explosion with slow-motion fire, and sprinklers bursting on over the Agents.
Pearl Harbor attack: vintage fighter planes overhead and through the surrounds, bombs falling on ships and igniting fires with deep rumble, gunshot ricochets, and exceptionally heavy bass throughout.

Chapters 12-13: the end-of-movie battle, with explosions and gunfire shifting overhead and whipping around the room and bullets whizzing past with precise placement. Among the best Atmos audio of 2024.
Kong's first appearance, when he hits the helicopter and the back rotor starts spinning around all the speakers.

Around the 50-min mark: eruption of liquid mud triggers a blowout with splattering sounds through every speaker, then ignition causes a massive explosion with ricocheting rivets, groaning girders and ferocious fires saturating the soundscape.
Famous one-shot sprint across the battlefield: grenades explode around the listener, bullets whistle overhead, soldiers shout from different directions.
End battle set to 80s music; just before it, a rocket shoots up and blows up the force field, crackle and explosion directly overhead. Less famous than the race but a strong demo moment.

movie_title: Star Wars: Episode I — The Phantom Menace
description: The podrace sequence, with podracer engines given particularly careful attention in the sound mix.

movie_title: Star Wars: Episode VII — The Force Awakens
description: Rey, Finn and BB-8 run toward the Millennium Falcon with TIE fighters flying directly overhead and precisely localized, then it continues inside the Falcon with TIE fighters all around plus deep bass.

Dramatic Zimmer/Wallfisch score pulsates as cars travel through the soundscape; K blasts them from the air, they crash into the water; waves crash over the vehicle and into the overheads as it submerges and the fight ensues.
Toward the end of the film, the rescue of children from the sea is impressive both technically and sonically, benefiting strongly from Atmos's 3D character.

Convoy of cars and trucks tearing across the desert: solid bass for engines, beating drums and the flame-thrower guitar through surrounds and heights, war boys' cheers and chants; vehicles collide with the buzzards with fire/explosions and circular-saw razor sounds.
Mysterio traps Spider-Man in a virtual world: Mysterio's voice travels all around, Spider-Man punches columns thinking they're Mysterio with structural collapse sounds, voices shift based on POV.
Thor suits up just before the big battle. Lightning cracks as he summons his weapons, with a full surround effect.

K approaches the abandoned casino: distant echoes and environmental hums layer over a sense of a forgotten city; soft whine of old holograms drifts through the room, tiny mechanical sounds ping from above.
Rockets flying all around makes you feel like you're right in the middle of everything.
Sammy summons spirits past, present and future; ethereal vocals soar and the camera swoops around dancing souls in the juke joint.
The naval bombardment that opens the ridge assault, with destroyer guns pounding the Japanese positions before the infantry attack.

movie_title: Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World
description: First encounter between HMS Surprise and Acheron: 18-pounders boom from distant fog, rounds splinter and shatter the Surprise's deck.
K and Joi fly through a storm: rain on wipers, distant thunder, bullets streaking the room, then near-silence as lightning cuts the power.
From the 32:25 mark: quiet hangar chat snaps into a siren-blaring time-jump portal that fills the ceiling with roaring audio.
The storm hits with relentless use of the surrounds and overheads; individual ice and wind elements swirl distinctly around and above for a chilling sense of being trapped on the mountain.
A plane flies directly overhead during the car show: a clean, striking workout for the height channels.
T. rex breaks out of its cage in the rain.
Americans bomb Japanese ships; retaliatory big-gun thumps and whizzing bullets surround the cockpit from every angle.
Swarming drones whizz overhead while the President and an agent plunge underwater to evade a drone bomb. The surrounds simulate the pressure and the explosion above is precisely placed.
Rose plays piano downstairs while Phil mockingly plays banjo from the rear ceiling, his roaming spurs filling the overheads before his boots shock her.
The film's long opening car chase: a frenetic, gunfire-filled pursuit through the streets of Florence.

scene_name: The Great Before vs New York
description: Two contrasting sonic worlds: ethereal springy reverb of the great before vs the tactile pile-driver-and-jazz cacophony of autumnal New York.
Opening: Kirk and McCoy chased through the forest by natives (sides for trees, spears in sides/surrounds), then Spock dropped into an erupting volcano, then USS Enterprise rises out of the water.
Jack-Jack first enters another dimension: a giggling baby crawls around the ceiling from speaker to speaker, very specific sound placement that isn't lost in the chaos.
Mine shaft starts collapsing on the two main characters after the big explosion the rat caused by running through the trip wire.

Stone enters the ISS: sub channel beats a heartbeat pulse, breathing and small debris sounds inside the cluttered cabin; alarms blare through overhead speakers when fire breaks out until she hits her head and all audio ceases.
The bubbleship pursuit, with pronounced height sounds: rain, lightning, water and flight through rugged terrain.
A Le Mans race moment. Engine roars and explosions build a thumping soundtrack that makes you feel like you're driving the race yourself.

scene_name: Alone Time with Henry Ford II
description: Shifts from subtle ambient track sounds (planes, distant mechanics) to the violent mechanical roar of the GT40, balancing Ford II's terrified screams against high-SPL engine noise.
From the get-go: nervous soldiers on a plane rattle through the air; right in the middle of every bullet and explosion.
Axe strikes ring out across the soundstage, each impact landing distinctly in the front and rear surround channels.
Trees burn in the field, the crackle of fire placed convincingly overhead in the height channels.

Pouring rain through heights/surrounds, looming UFO presence as the area loses power; eerie screams move from rear surrounds to heights as the UFO engulfs the soundstage; debris descends on the house, then outside with Daniel Kaluuya in the car for rain, thunder and haunting rumbles.

Around 30 min: tanks drive off the road and onto the battlefield with low-end rumble and chatter in surrounds; eruption of machine-gun fire with metallic ricochet clanging, machine gunner blasts from heights, main tank gun booms, enemy anti-tank rounds whistle, all under Steven Price's score.
Around the 3-minute mark, set to Led Zeppelin's 'Whole Lotta Love': cars scream past through surrounds, radio chatter crackles, fireworks explode overhead in the height channels.
Spartans shield themselves from arrows from above: arrows whistle through the air and land in side/rear surrounds, then pound on shields activating overhead channels.
Multiple Pandora-underwater scenes from ~1h onward: whale songs float through the room, air bubbles rise audibly, ocean currents envelop the listener.

A silent leadup to the assassination shot, then a jarring gunshot impact kicks off the action through a techno-thumping nightclub and into the catacombs chase, with multiple gun signatures (machine guns, shotguns) all around.

The villain's giant robot at the end: the cloning villain laughs and screams while bouncing all around the room, then a huge explosion when the robot falls. Strong room-bouncing localization plus heavy bass.

movie_title: 13 Hours: The Secret Soldiers of Benghazi
description: The attack on the compound, building to a bus blown up with heavy ordnance; bullets fly right past the head.
An excellent all-around sound bubble as Doc Ock shows off his arms and fires up the fusion reactor, the lasers firing with a percussive thump.
Vocals and dynamics. Not a bass demo but a showcase for natural vocal reproduction on a well-balanced system.
A race with roaring engines, peeling tires and cornering detail; when cars hit the rumble strips beside the track you hear the tire tone shift, plus dirt and gravel flying across the soundfield.
The light-cycle arena battle: crisp, geometric sound design set to Daft Punk's score, with a very powerful, room-shaking low end.

scene_name: Rodan's attack on Isla de Mara
description: Rodan chasing the fighter jets and meeting Monster Zero.

movie_title: All Quiet on the Western Front
scene_name: First few minutes in the war
description: The opening battle, when a bomb blows up next to a running soldier and you hear the rubble rain down above you.
Motorcycles weave with clean left-to-right motion; police sirens ricochet between buildings with metallic sharpness; engines rev and shift directions with pinpoint accuracy.

movie_title: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
description: The Battle of Helm's Deep, the night siege of the fortress, with the remastered mix driving rain, Uruk-hai roars and the wall breach through every channel.
The protagonists are almost captured by Klingons just before Khan shows up; top-tier sound and image.
Chapter 14/22. Officer K investigates a beehive, a quiet scene save for one dramatic bass note. The immersive Atmos mix is famous for making demo audiences swat at the air around them.
The goblin-tunnel chase, with thunderous bass and strong height effects as the rickety walkways collapse.
From the Universal Studios logo onward, the opening builds an enveloping, immersive Atmos atmosphere.

Aircraft flight to Antarctica (engine rumble through the heights and surrounds), Ospreys deploy with thunderous blade slap, facility echo, firefight, ice-wall bomb detonation, Ghidorah awakens with roars and lightning blasts, then Godzilla shows up for a battle with an aircraft missile barrage.
The Hong Kong battle: Gipsy Danger versus the kaiju Otachi, the fight tearing through the city with debris and impacts tracking across the surround and height channels.
The scene with the trash pandas (raccoons) on the roof.

movie_title: Rogue One: A Star Wars Story
scene_name: Rocks falling after Death Star shot test
description: Escape from Saw's hideout, where Atmos makes it feel like the entire cave is crumbling around the listener.

movie_title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
description: Caverns, slaughtered dwarves, orcs surrounding the Fellowship, arrows flying, the cave-troll fight, then the Balrog stomping in. A longtime demo favourite that works the sides, surrounds and subwoofer.

The opening Buzz Lightyear sequence (later revealed to be a video game): flying through space, a planet opening up, light tunnels, and a fight with Emperor Zurg and his Death Star-like power orb. Fun for the sides, surrounds and subwoofer.
Damon and Affleck talk to a girl in the room while the crew demolishes a wall one floor up; thuds land in the top channel.
Glitch effects and dimensional rips bounce around in a kaleidoscope of motion; punches, web swings and energy bursts track across height channels.
Lead-up begins around the 59-minute mark with a child's singing only Poirot can hear; bassy thumps, disembodied voices, wild woodwinds and a raging storm.
Sunny summer street of children and chatter morphs into the swirling low-toned chaos of a riot; rocks fly overhead as a bin lid becomes a shield.
A bomb hits the high-ceilinged Vatican mid-vote; tense strings cut out, debris falls and the building's collapse fills the room.
Harkonnen ambush: thrumming ornithopters and a missile barrage give way to silent sand cloud, then Fremen warriors and room-filling chanting.
Evelyn's final showdown in the doughnut-shaped abyss: whooshing and swirling sweep around as dialogue threads through the chaos.
Sailors find a wounded Frankenstein on the tundra; sled dogs, fire crackle, whistling wind, then the Creature's deep growl and a bone-cracking rampage from all angles.
Climactic Le Mans race fills the room with crowd noise, a stunt jet fly-by and revving engines; strong dynamics and bass weight.

movie_title: Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny
description: Cave chapter with underwater burbling effects and a brief gunfight where bullets whizz around and behind the listening position.
Latter third builds into sustained bedlam with every sound placed slightly elevated and tremendous low-end effects to test the subwoofer.
Ambush at Vesper's tomb leaves Bond deafened; chase ends with rain of bullets on the Aston Martin panned across interior and exterior, interwoven with churchbells.
Around the 72-minute mark: car chase to Pat Benatar's 'Heartbreaker' becomes an R-rated Home Alone in a warehouse, with flying bullets, shrapnel and explosions.
Quiet desert ambience, gravel crunch and uneasy snorts build to a bassy jump scare; voices echo across the landscape and the horse can no longer be seen.
A pack of Count Orlok's wolves attacks; carriage rumble and snarling rise as the danger closes in.
Miles flees Miguel O'Hara across the frame; energetic score and pinpoint placement track him vertically and around the soundfield.
Mall battle against possessed electronics: soda-can missiles, whizzing drones, raining Furbies and a Godzilla-Furby crescendo using zany height effects.
Team escapes an underground lair under directional gunfire, with a supersonic-flight blast for low-end heft and a pounding score on top.
Bass-heavy LA showdown driven by Dr. Dre / Snoop Dogg / Cypress Hill tracks; thunderous gunshots throughout the action-packed finale.
Ethiopian quarry exterior segues into the deep reverb of the mine; synth-heavy score bursts off-screen and threads ingeniously into Howard's world.
Alpha Two fights through Ramadi streets to reach Alpha One: gunfire flies precisely across and above; Mk 46 machine gun moves the subwoofer.
Elphaba belts the title song atop the turret; guards bang at the doors and she plummets through wind on her broom with voices from all sides.
Scene in the beginning where she walks under the police robot — among the best for any Atmos movie.
Scene where Maverick steals the F-18 to prove he can fly the training course.
Chapter 3: skydiving sequence — a workout for every speaker.
Title fight scene in Deadpool — opening freeway fight during the credits.
Whispers, distant thumps and layered chanting spiral around just above the listener's head; soft breaths and shifting fabric sit close to the ear — ritual-like and intimate.
Opening at the carnival: side rides overhead, food machines and game noises envelop the viewer while opening-credits music keeps dialogue separated.
OP — Bass category: boat battle scene with eerie deep magnet sounds — sub workout.
OP — Full Dynamic Range category: Maverick flying the canyon, no music throughout — just the awesome power of the jet.

Opening: stadium atmosphere places the listener in the middle of the audience; bass drum at ~50 sec hits hard, screaming guitar elevated overhead, Cooper's voice centered; at 02:25 Bradley slams the corridor shut and the concert vacuum-cuts to silence.
OP: Bethany gets eaten by the hippo and respawns — cool audio 'drop'.
OP: same kind of audio drop effect when Fridge eats cake and dies.
OP: definite height effects with all the coins being thrown around by Doc Ock.

scene_name: Big reactor powerup and final battle
description: OP: not as much height effect, but the overall mix is still really great.
Relies on absence of sound as much as presence: subtle creeping creature cues placed terrifyingly precisely in the surround channels.
'Let It Be' sequence flashes between the 1967 Detroit riots and the Vietnam War; gospel choir vocals over the funerals of two killed characters — hauntingly plaintive.

Start of chapter 2 through Harker's arrival: fly buzzes circumferentially and overhead, asylum moans emanate from all walls, wolves stalk the coach with thunder cracking overhead, then atmospheric drips, rats and wailing souls fill Dracula's castle.
Eerie sand groan and subtle desert wind build a massive sense of space; chanting rises from all angles before erupting into a dynamic, deep-bass action set piece.
Zero-G training exercise (Space-Age 'capture the flag'): things happen in all directions and the disorientation reads through a good system. Family-friendly action with no blood.
Gosling in a tight capsule re-entering Earth's atmosphere: claustrophobic clatters and beeps surround the viewer, intensified by Atmos.
Tris taunted by Jeanine: Jeanine's voice placed in the ceiling matching her POV; Tris dives through glass and falls into a 3D-overhead sim of a collapsing city with debris and explosions all around.

scene_name: Amity Sim — part 2 (Good Tris vs Evil Tris)
description: Concluding ~10 minutes after part 1: Evil Tris jumps through glass, slams Good Tris through walls; Matrix-style superhuman battle through walls and floors of the collapsing city.
Crashing waves and surf all around; dialogue swirls 360° as a character turns to listen to people talking — also exposes any speaker timbre-matching issues.
Water drips from overhead in the cave complex — Atmos used for vertical ambience.
Hotel lobby Muzak pumps out of the ceiling speakers as if walking through the hotel.

Earthquake sequence cutting between restaurant, Caltech offices and a San Francisco office building/garage collapse; height channels carry falling debris, groaning girders and helicopter blades; ends with a chunk of building striking the helicopter, spinning the soundfield.

scene_name: Battle of the bands vs. Katayanagi Twins
description: New Atmos remix is loud and bold — battle between Sex Bob-Omb and the Katayanagi Twins reveals nuances and details that were buried in the original surround mix's subwoofer assault.

movie_title: Star Wars: Episode V — The Empire Strikes Back
description: Hoth blizzard whips wind and snow around the room; mighty AT-AT walker foot stomps deliver deep, powerful bass.

movie_title: Star Wars: Episode V — The Empire Strikes Back
description: Immersive jungle ambience with creature noises and rustling leaves, plus a brief rainstorm that showers the room.

movie_title: Star Wars: Episode V — The Empire Strikes Back
description: Probe droids launched from the Star Destroyer whiz across the ceiling right from the film's start.

Chapter 11, ~7-minute attack on Felix, Terrier and Annie; shattering glass, splintering wood and falling brass placed precisely, culminating in a bathroom inferno that uses height channels to billow fire overhead and across the room.
Subtle suspense opens into a swirling-heights, deep-bass transportation sequence; on arrival the soundstage opens up wide and airy.
OP: bear fight scene at 48:38.
Around 2h 13min: a large explosion and ensuing battle; sound dances throughout the different speakers and places the listener in the middle of the action.

Opening: placed in the woods with insects and birds flying all around using every speaker; height speakers send small wildlife sounds across the room. Author notes the Atmos mix is much cleaner on Kaleidescape/Blu-ray than the Max stream.
Opening scene: team chases a massive tornado; bed-layer channels carry the whipping wind while Atmos overheads handle rain and effects in the distance above.
Opening sequence at 0:30 — had author reach for the remote as the whole house shook from the LFE.

Whole intro with Groot dancing while the team fights a giant alien: music, explosions, lasers, swords; later Peter flies speaker-to-speaker asking each teammate if they have tape — pure localization demo.
Kids on a metal scaffolding bridge inside the burning building: a brief silence breaks as the ceiling literally cracks and breaks directly above the listener — only sound at that moment.

movie_title: Star Wars: Episode VII — The Force Awakens
scene_name: Han Solo discovers them — grate scene
description: Han Solo's freighter finds the Falcon: while they hide in a hole, Han literally rips a grate off the floor (their ceiling) — author calls out this overhead localization as a standout demo moment.

Opening dinner with the dwarves crashing Bilbo's home: at the original Dolby Atmos premiere, author leaned forward twice telling people in his theater to be quiet — extreme localization made it sound like real people in the room.
About an hour in: trolls talk directly overhead as if the listener is a hobbit and they're towering above — strong localization in the height channels.
~2:15 flying sequence around the 19-min mark: subtle voices showing off the centre channel; author notes it's not heavy on top effects but still strong.
Mr. Bean (Rowan Atkinson) opens the door and a giraffe — much taller than him — snorts and makes noises right above the listener with strong overhead placement.

scene_name: Doors crash down sealing them in
description: OP: 'they come to the room and find themselves locked in and all the doors come crashing down around to seal them in'.

scene_name: Terminator on top of the school bus
description: OP: 'they are in a school bus and bad terminator walks on top of the bus — you can hear the ceiling denting in above you'.
Wakanda battle ground.
Hallway fight sequence from Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3.
First successful flight with Toothless.
The literal beginning of Star Wars: A New Hope (4K release with Atmos).
Rainy subway introduction to Batman — great for just rain falling above you.
Thor arriving in Wakanda — a great surround moment.

movie_title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
description: Fellowship of the Ring - Watcher in the Water scene.
Graffiti scene — different music parts coming from every direction yet distinct; one of the best Atmos demos.
Mad-Max-like intro to the digital space — good use of 3D audio and the NIN soundtrack bust in.

movie_title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
description: Fellowship of the Ring Prologue — Sauron explodes scene.
Same as bike race — Master Audio up-mixes beautifully, very powerful LFE.
Debrief scene near the beginning of the film (K reporting to Lt. Joshi).
H goes into room 237 with the naked zombie, hits his head and enters the maze — all axe swings clearly above.
Lady Gaga at the piano: subtle nuances — fingers on keys, lips parting — over a wide female vocal range; great test for music in a dedicated theater.

High-energy ambush with explosions, sniper rifle ricochets, a flamethrower across the truck cab with deep bass, then the truck hits a tower (THX-style bass drop). Standout overhead moment: gun shells roll across the height channels and drop down onto the platform.
Subtle piano-driven build into Jenny Lind's soaring female vocal — chill-bump moment as the volume of sound in the room peaks.
First 5 minutes — Godzilla's rumble from above as he sniffs the airplane the main character is hiding in.

movie_title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
description: Gandalf scolding Bilbo at Bag End: rafters creaking and Gandalf's voice envelops the room.
'Sin Voice' scene — short and intense.

scene_name: Earth Scene to End of Test Run Failure
description: Earth scene through the end of the test run failure.
Deus Ex Machina sequence.
Opening battle with Blackout (helicopter) and subsequent desert battle.
Scene during a car chase where a helicopter flies overhead — sounds like a chopper is going to land in the living room with ceiling speakers.

scene_name: Skydiving intro — fireworks and stage landing
description: Intro with fireworks as he is skydiving, and when he lands on the stage — really good experience.
Scene where John runs through the building with the shotgun shooting fireshells, filmed from above — gorgeous on OLED.
First half is deliberately subdued; halfway through, when the character experiences a life-changing revelation, the mix opens right up — using sound design to add depth to the storytelling.
The environment boiling while engrossing chants elevate the sound of clashing blades — author's 'go-to Atmos scene'.

scene_name: Kid falls down in hole in garage
description: When the kid falls down in the hole in the garage.
When the town square is shelled.
The whole last fight has lots of really pronounced Atmos effects.
The beginning when Rocket speaks above Nebula — pronounced Atmos.
Scene where they come to abduct the girl from the high-rise building — non-stop panning left/right and front/back.
Right in the beginning where all the airplanes fly over.
Running through the tunnel.
Extremely active height channels in the forest scene.
The fight at the beginning when he summons the lightning.

scene_name: Throws the bike above his head
description: When he throws the bike above his head.
The final battle sequence.
Saw it in theater with HFR and Atmos — heard 'someone' snoring behind him so vividly he turned to wake them up; it was the dwarves on screen.
At the very end of the credits, just as the end title music has faded out, a quiet slithery, chittering noise plays just over the listener's head.
Patrick Bateman's voice narration throughout the film is played through the height channels.
Battle scene in the neon city — pretty visually spectacular.
Diamond Luxe Atmos version: the return-to-earth re-entry sequence — author's favorite alongside the ISS.
John Wick 1 4K UHD: rain falling during Helen's funeral — Atmos content is constant in that scene, useful for setting Atmos levels.

scene_name: Creature jumps on roof, kids knock over oil lamp
description: Creature jumps on the roof and the kids knock over an oil lamp — convincing overhead sound.
Opening scene with him in the junkyard — great atmospheric from heights.
Quiet scene where they get out of the boat and walk into the jungle; subtle jungle noises all around and above.
First race through the big crash — engine hum in the sub, crowd in surrounds, cars flying by on both sides.
The stadium scene in Dune Part 2.
The kid goes to retrieve dice and the ceiling starts to creak — convincing overhead sound.
First 9 minutes of Oblivion.

movie_title: War for the Planet of the Apes
description: Climax: a helicopter flies toward the screen and really sounds like it's above you — first time author experienced overhead Atmos effect from Sonos Arc.
Not Atmos (5.1 only). End-of-movie gunfight: bad guys vs police, all guns ringing in the ears and surrounds — author rates it as comparable to the Heat gunfight scene.

movie_title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
scene_name: Cornish pixies in Defense Against the Dark Arts
description: Lockhart releases Cornish pixies in the DADA class; little blue creatures fly all over carrying children up to the ceiling — sides/surrounds full of creature sounds, plus the falling skeleton's heights and low end.
Superman vs Zod destroys a small town: heights when Superman launches, sides/surrounds as they fly through cornfield, jets and helicopters coming in, guns firing down the road.

movie_title: Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith
description: Anakin and Obi-Wan in the massive opening space battle: ships whizz by, laser blasters firing, explosions; 360° bubble of sound surrounds the listener.
Military announcement causes a stampede of alien creatures activating surrounds and overheads; a second stampede follows as a helicopter makes another announcement and stirs the creatures again.
Full dynamics across the bed-layer speakers: enemy fire originates from the right side and right rear; height channels stay in the background here.
Actor looks up to the ceiling and is met with the image of herself strapped in a seatbelt — gruesome scene that pans audio back and forth from ceiling to screen.
Arrows scream past the ears in side and rear surrounds; crumbling rocks from above after the exploding arrows hit.
3:28 clip: Blake's hearing is heightened and he hears stomping coming from upstairs — author calls this 'over the top Atmos'.
2:38 clip: creaking trees and movement in the woods using the height and surround speakers.
41-second clip: described as crazy use of the left surround only.
Sneaking through the corridor infested with Parasitoids/Facehuggers — in cinema author thought there was something crawling on the ceiling. The 4K Blu-Ray reproduces this well at home.
Haitian trap house gun fight.
Blade Runner 2049 end credits.
Attack on Sinuiju.
The Gemini 8 launch scene — starts at about 45 minutes in.
Underrated chase scene; the movie is also 60fps which adds intensity.
Second altercation with the King (Godzilla).

movie_title: Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire
description: Fight in Cairo.
The Wolfpack attacks the convoy.
When they arrive at Villain-Con: announcements play overhead — author always looks around the room confused for a second.

scene_name: Ethan Hunt conversation with the entity in the pod
description: Scene where Ethan Hunt has the conversation with the entity in the pod — 'sounds insanely good'.
Helicopter flying around you — great demo for Atmos immersion.

scene_name: Radio comms with the control room
description: Any time Tom Cruise radios to the woman in the control room.
Bombs going off all over the place in the first fight scene.
Killing of Gregori Rasputin — sync to 1812 Overture is very nicely done.
From the 1 hr mark and the next 22 minutes — author notes ironically that a 22-minute chunk obviously has more atmospheric sound but still calls it 'the best Atmos demo ever'.
Second scene: right when they kill the power.

scene_name: Roller coaster to meet Grandmaster — overhead announcer
description: Thor on the roller coaster to meet Jeff Goldblum: female announcer narrates the events to Thor straight out of the ceiling speakers.
About 55 minutes in — the tops are going crazy. Author calls this demo material.
EF5 Tornado in El Reno — unique sounds.
